experiment.steer: S015 §9 delete the CUDA-era copy; §125 unified memory as a weapon; §77 the metric that counts

kernel.note: native matvec and pack MSL byte-identical to two blocks ago; what moved is WHERE THE OPERANDS LIVE

headline: THE BYTES STOPPED COMING HOME. Three arms separate two changes: the GATE moving to the device (+58.31%) and the OPERANDS staying there (+113.86% on top). 635,422 -> 1,005,946 -> 2,151,304 WorkUnits/hour, 3.39x end to end, every arm inside the 10% IQR gate and both steps completely separated.

three_arms_because_two_things_changed.A: host gate -- the float64 CPU gate from the previous block
three_arms_because_two_things_changed.B: device gate -- both matvecs in MLX primitives, true tensor copied to device per tensor
three_arms_because_two_things_changed.C: B plus residency -- pack outputs stay on device, bf16 decoded there too
three_arms_because_two_things_changed.why_not_one_arm: collapsing them would have reported 3.39x as 'the gate moved to the GPU', which is false: the gate move is 1.58x of it and residency is 2.14x.

the_untouched_kernels_got_faster_and_tha.pack_s: 0.05549 -> 0.01691 = 3.28x running THE SAME MSL. Two thirds of the pack column was the device->host->device round trip the GPU-pack receipt explicitly listed as NOT DONE.
the_untouched_kernels_got_faster_and_tha.gpu_s: 0.03707 -> 0.02362 = 1.57x running THE SAME MSL, because mx.array(packed) was being charged to that column.
the_untouched_kernels_got_faster_and_tha.decode_s: 0.07637 -> 0.00558 = 13.68x. This column DID NOT EXIST before -- it was most of the ~19% the previous receipt reported as unaccounted, and it was the CPU bf16 upcast. On device it is a VIEW, not a conversion.
the_untouched_kernels_got_faster_and_tha.read_s: 0.03453 -> 0.03163 = 1.09x, untouched code again slightly faster, the same cross-phase effect the previous receipt measured.

prediction_written_before_the_run.falsifier: if C is not clearly better than B, residency is not the lever

prediction_verdict.falsifier_survived: C had to be clearly better than B or residency was not the lever; it is 2.14x better with complete separation
prediction_verdict.five_in_a_row: FIVE CONSECUTIVE PREDICTIONS IN THIS PIPELINE HAVE COME IN ABOVE THEIR BAND (Tier 1, GPU pack, honest gate, and now both arms here). The previous receipt named cross-phase interference and that is real but small (~6.5%). THE LARGER MECHANISM IS VISIBLE HERE: I predict by subtracting the cost of the thing I am removing, and a host round trip is not charged to one column -- it was spread across decode, pack and gpu, three columns I was holding fixed. Removing a COPY removes cost from every phase that was paying for it.
prediction_verdict.what_would_fix_the_method: predict from a phase decomposition that has NO unaccounted remainder. A's remainder was 19% before decode_s was split out, and the miss was roughly that size.

resident_path_bit_identity.means: device bf16 decode + device pack are BIT-IDENTICAL to the host path

correctness_is_the_precondition_and_it_i.what_the_device_gate_cannot_claim: the numbers are NOT identical -- float32 accumulation disagrees with the float64 host gate by up to 2.85e-06 on cosine and 7.62e-07 on the magnitude ratio, an ORDER ABOVE the 1e-7 a single rounding would suggest because error accumulates through a 32-term inner product and a per-group sum. What IS claimed is the verdicts: 96 calls, 32 negative controls, zero mismatches, and the tightest honest verdict sits 0.00289 from its threshold = 1013x the worst disagreement. near_threshold_headroom() reports that distance with EVERY verdict, and a test pins that it says NO when the margin is thin.
correctness_is_the_precondition_and_it_i.the_independence_question_answered_preci: moving the reference onto the same device does NOT make gate 1 vacuous, but the reason matters: gate 1 compares the hand-written MSL against MLX PRIMITIVES -- different code, different compiled kernels, different arithmetic structure. What gate 1 never checked, in ANY version including the numpy one, is the NIBBLE CONVENTION, which both sides always shared. A convention error is caught by GATE 2 against the true tensor, which is exactly what the `nibbles swapped` control demonstrates. Stating that is the difference between a defensible move and a quiet weakening.

claim_boundary.clean: A 2.52%, B 5.86%, C 4.04% spread, all inside the 10% gate; B over A and C over B both COMPLETELY SEPARATED; 6 rounds of 3 arms, warmed twice.
claim_boundary.reps: 6 samples per arm, still below the 200-rep bar the program's own stability audit sets for a RELIABILITY VERDICT.
claim_boundary.baseline_reproduced: arm A measures 635,422 WU/h against 634,259 recorded in a different process last block -- 0.18% apart.
claim_boundary.not_shown: no kernel changed, so no Metal performance claim moves. The gate is now float32 and must not be used on a pack whose verdict sits within ~3e-04 of a threshold; the host float64 gate remains the reference and both are kept. Nothing here says ws_rtn_q4_g64 is adequate for a MODEL -- local adequacy does not compose.
claim_boundary.what_is_left: with the remainder gone the phases are verify 27.1%, read 29.5%, pack 15.8%, gpu 22.1%, decode 5.2%. READ IS NOW THE LARGEST SINGLE PHASE AGAIN at 0.0316 s, and it is a page-cached read of 192 MB, so the next honest lever is either a bigger working set that does not fit the cache or accepting that this pipeline is now storage-bound at Tier 1 speeds.
